summary: The current-API equivalent of the original vector bitwise-not reproduction already compiles and matches Torch exactly on the prepared base. The candidate's signed/unsigned vector invert and negate GPU tests also pass unchanged on base, so the candidate does not cause those paths to start working. It adds strong regression coverage and changes Python logical not on Vector from silent truth evaluation to a clear TypeError; that diagnostic is the only failing-before/passing-after behavior found.

tests.what_was_measured: Literal source compatibility; compilation stopped before the unary operation because current make_tile rejects a list argument.

tests.command: FLYDSL_DUMP_IR=1 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-cb67f37a134f/venv/bin/python /job/evidence-j-cb67f37a134f/vector_unary_original.py (make_tile spelling adapted to current API, base checkout)
tests.what_was_measured: Original 8x24 tiled-copy shape and 15-block launch executed on GPU; output was exactly equal to Torch bitwise inversion.
400 tests passed, including four real-GPU signed/unsigned int32 boundary cases compared exactly with NumPy.
The candidate GPU regression passed unchanged on base: 4 passed, showing vector invert/negate behavior predates the candidate.
Candidate diagnostic regression failed on base because Python not on Vector did not raise TypeError; this test passes on candidate.
Four uncached GPU cases passed; MLIR used vector<48xi32> xori/subi and final gfx950 ISA used v_not_b32_e32/v_sub_u32_e32.

gpu_evidence: Torch saw one AMD Instinct MI350X with capability (9, 5); exact GPU outputs matched Torch/NumPy and complete gfx950 ISA dumps are retained under /job/evidence-j-cb67f37a134f/.
remaining_limitations: The assigned device was MI350X gfx950 with ROCm/HIP 7.2, not the reported MI355 with ROCm 7.1. The literal historical script requires a make_tile API spelling adaptation before reaching unary compilation. No candidate C++ files changed, so the prepared pinned-wheel native compiler was used and no rebuild was applicable.
